title: The tree that configures the fleet
dek: Chromium's CI is 1,211 builders in 18 buckets, all of them generated by lucicfg from 125 Starlark files inside the repository they build. This is how a change gets from git cl upload to refs/heads/main, how 2.4 million test tasks a day get scheduled, and how a milestone turns into a branch, a version bump and a release.
byline: 22 September 2026 · Subject: chromium/src@f288fed6 (156.0.8067.0), depot_tools@0306e468 and v8@15.6.0 (standalone; this Chromium pins 15.6.19)
description: Chromium's 1,211 builders, its commit queue and its release branches are all generated by lucicfg from 125 Starlark files in the tree.
og_description: A teardown of Chromium's CI/CD: the LUCI stack, infra/config Starlark and the generated cfgs, tests on bots, bot_update, the commit queue, tree closers and gardeners, the two-week release cycle and the release scripts.

sections.title: Four pipelines on one substrate
sections.brief: THESIS: Chromium's "CI/CD" is not one pipeline but four, and the only thing that makes them one system is that all four are configured from files checked into chromium/src itself. Say that first; the rest of the post is the proof. The four (dossier §1.1): pre-submit verifies every CL; post-submit rebuilds and retests every commit on refs/heads/main; a performance pipeline measures a much smaller set of commits on real hardware; a release pipeline cuts branches, bumps versions, pins dependencies and packages binaries. Facts and quotes. LUCI is "a collection of CI services that run on Google Cloud [which] form the backbone of Chromium's CI system" [src/docs/infra/glossary.md:101-102] from the docs. Quote the glossary's three definitions verbatim and in order: a Build is "A Buildbucket job that runs a single CI-specific task"; a Builder is "A named configuration (or grouping) of builds in Buildbucket"; and "As of writing (Q3 2022), all Buildbucket builds are themselves Swarming tasks" [glossary.md:10-20]. Then check that last sentence against the tree instead of repeating it: `swarming_host: "chromium-swarm.appspot.com"` occurs 1,211 times in src/infra/config/generated/luci/cr-buildbucket.cfg, once per builder (re-verified locally at f288fed6) from the tree; a Q2-2025 doc raises it to "nearly 100% of Chromium infra workloads run as Swarming tasks" [src/docs/infra/builder_types.md:20-32]. Buildbot inheritance, one paragraph only. LUCI = "Layered Universal Continuous Integration"; it split Buildbot's monolithic masters into independent services, and masters survive only as UI "groups" [src/docs/tour_of_luci_ui.md:279-297]. On 25 September 2019 Eric Foo of Chrome Operations posted under the subject "Chrome is 100% on LUCI. Buildbot officially turned down": "Yesterday, we officially turned down the last Buildbot master and are now 100% on LUCI (ci.chromium.org) as the official build infrastructure for ChromeOS and Chrome official releases, CI/Waterfall, and CQ/tryjobs systems" [https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-dev/c/zS3R6IEN7X4/m/gYuWAZYtAQAJ]. Name two fossils the post collects later: `bot_update` still heads the tree-closing step regexp though it can no longer fire (§09), and //testing/buildbot still carries a waterfalls.pyl (§05). Set the reference frame explicitly: chromium/src@f288fed6 (chrome/VERSION 156.0.8067.0, refs/heads/main@{#1701190}, checked out 2026-09-18), depot_tools@0306e468, V8 15.6.0; live-service readings were taken 2026-09-18 to 09-22 and are dated where they appear, because they move. OWNED ELSEWHERE: builder counts beyond the 1,211 total (§03 owns buckets and groups); CQ numbers (§06); fleet numbers (§05); release dates and cadence (§10); script paths (§11).

Each service box carries the host pinned in src/infra/config/main.star:88-96 (cr-buildbucket.appspot.com, luci-logdog, luci-milo, luci-notify, luci-scheduler, chromium-swarm) plus CV's chromium-cq-status.appspot.com and luci-analysis.appspot.com. sections.title: The tree configures the fleet
sections.brief:
THESIS: //infra/config is a compiler. 125 Starlark files are executed by lucicfg into 3,555 generated files that the LUCI services then poll out of git. Nothing is deployed; a config change is a CL. Facts. //infra/config holds "the configuration for the LUCI services (also known as Chrome Operations) for the chromium project" [src/infra/config/README.md:6-25]. At f288fed6 it is itself a lucicfg package: PACKAGE.star declares `@chromium-project` with a minimum lucicfg of 1.44.1, two entry points (main.star, dev.star) and two dependencies — `@chromium-luci` from the separate infra/chromium repo pinned at 3c067cfcf061330718cee8a4c74d9cd7232595c6, and a local `@chromium-targets` rooted at infra/config/targets; PACKAGE.lock records lucicfg 1.46.7 [src/infra/config/PACKAGE.star:7-43; PACKAGE.lock:2-9]. One structural paragraph: on 2025-07-22 commit b711da6e4f deleted the whole infra/config/lib library — builders.star, ci.star, try.star, builder_config.star, gn_args.star, targets.star, bootstrap.star, branches.star, notifiers.star, orchestrator.star — replacing it with `load("@chromium-luci//ci.star", "ci")` imports so chromium and the internal chrome project share one library [https://github.com/chromium/chromium/commit/b711da6e4f]. What remains in lib/ is constants: CI defaults (recipe `chromium`, 3-hour timeout, pool luci.chromium.ci), try defaults (`chromium_trybot`, 4 hours), Siso job tiers 250/80/500/150/-1, Xcode 27.0 RC `27a266a`, twelve gardener rotations, and exemption lists that "should *only* decrease" [lib/ci_constants.star:5-14; try_constants.star:5-10; siso.star:5-21; builder_exemptions.star:5-11]. main.star is the contract: it pins lucicfg, enables the crbug.com/1182002 Scheduler experiment, and calls `lucicfg.config(config_dir = "generated", fail_on_warnings = True)` with a `tracked_files` manifest naming every artefact it owns — the service cfgs, `builders/*/*/*`, `builder-owners/*.txt`, `cq-builders.md`, `cq-usage/*`, `health-specs`, `sheriff-rotations/*.txt`, `outages.pyl`, `testing/*.pyl` [main.star:27-68]. Three files (testhaus.cfg, luci-analysis.cfg, luci-bisection.cfg) are hand-written and merely copied by `lucicfg.emit` [main.star:70-86]. Numbers, all re-verified locally: 125 .star files / 76,580 lines in; generated/ 3,555 files / 53 MB out. cr-buildbucket.cfg 139,286 lines / 5,544,282 bytes (5.29 MiB, which `ls -lh` prints as 5.3M, = 5.54 MB decimal — quote the bytes, dossier R03); commit-queue.cfg 9,451; luci-milo.cfg 31,964 / 90 consoles; luci-scheduler.cfg 7,092 / 697 jobs / 5 triggers; luci-notify.cfg 6,013 / 252 notifiers / 133 tree closers; realms.cfg 933 / 27 realms. How it reaches the services (§1.4). LUCI Config (config.luci.app) runs an import cron that spreads one task per config set over a 10-minute window, asks Gitiles for the latest commit touching the path, and commits the revision only if every service's `ValidateConfigs` returns no ERROR [luci-go config_service/internal/importer/importer.go]. On 2026-09-22 `projects/chromium` was imported from refs/heads/main path infra/config/generated/luci at f7de74e13efc (08:25:50Z), `lastImportAttempt: Up-to-date`. Consumers poll every minute, so a landed CL is live in roughly 1-11 minutes — mark reconstruction: derived from cron constants, never observed end to end. Presubmit runs the same validator earlier via `CheckLucicfgGenOutput` → `lucicfg validate main.star` [depot_tools/presubmit_canned_checks.py:3744-3778], and four verifier trybots (branch-config-verifier, builder-config-verifier, gn-args-verifier, targets-config-verifier) guard the per-builder files [try/presubmit.star:41-176]. CODE EXCERPT (1): src/infra/config/main.star:36-68 — `lucicfg.config(...)` with its tracked_files manifest, condensed to ≤ 25 lines with an elision marker. Escape < > & inside 
.
OWNED ELSEWHERE: the builder call and its expansion (§03); targets/ (§05); the CQ config groups (§06); branch-day regeneration (§10); recipe and binary propagation (§11).

sections.title: One builder, expanded
sections.brief:
THESIS: a CI builder is one keyword-argument call in Starlark and nine artefacts out; at run time it is a Swarming task whose command is a recipe it does not pin. Walk `ci/Linux Builder`, because every other builder is a variation of it. The call [src/infra/config/subprojects/chromium/ci/chromium.linux.star:328-378]: `ci.builder(name = "Linux Builder", ...)` names a builder_spec (gclient chromium + use_clang_coverage, chromium config + mb, RELEASE, 64-bit, LINUX), a six-entry gn_args.config (gpu_tests, release_builder, remoteexec, devtools_do_typecheck, linux, x64), a targets.bundle, a console entry (category "release", short name "bld") and a contact e-mail. Pool, cores, OS, gardener rotation, tree-closing and timeout are inherited from the file's `ci.defaults` and ci.star's bucket-wide defaults [chromium.linux.star:20-44; ci.star:16-26,73-115]. What lucicfg emits: a Buildbucket builder block, a Scheduler job, Milo console entries, a luci-notify tree_closer, a health spec, a builder-owners line, and four per-builder files — properties.json, shadow-properties.json, gn-args.json, targets/chromium.linux.json. The generated block [generated/luci/cr-buildbucket.cfg:17817-17845, re-verified]: seven dimensions — `builderless:1`, `cores:8`, `cpu:x86-64`, `free_space:standard`, `os:Ubuntu-22.04`, `pool:luci.chromium.ci`, `ssd:0` — and an `exe` that is not a recipe: cipd_package `infra/chromium/bootstrapper/${platform}`, cipd_version `latest`, cmd `bootstrapper`. The recipe bundle hides in the `$bootstrap/exe` property at `refs/heads/main`; `$bootstrap/properties` names `infra/config/generated/builders/ci/Linux Builder/properties.json`. Why: the bootstrapper reads that properties file from the source revision being built and applies the CL's diff to it, so a CQ run exercises the property change in its own CL [infra/chromium starlark-libs/chromium-luci/bootstrap.star:5-18]. Counts re-verified locally: 1,070 of 1,211 builders use the bootstrapper, 141 run `cmd: "luciexe"` directly. One consequence: neither an orchestrator nor the compilator it schedules pins the bundle — ScheduleBuildRequest.exe supports only cipd_version overrides — so they can run different recipe revisions reconstruction. At run time. A Buildbucket build is a Swarming task [src/docs/infra/builder_types.md:42-52]. Swarming is "purely a task scheduler service" with "a legion of dumb bots" matched by dimensions; a pool is a security boundary and file I/O goes through RBE-CAS, the successor of isolate [glossary.md:129-149]. On the bot, bbagent runs a LogDog butler, merges build.proto datagrams from the luciexe and forwards them to Buildbucket and Milo; a luciexe exiting without a terminal status is an INFRA_FAILURE [luci-go luciexe/doc.go]. The buckets, one paragraph plus the figure: ci 641, try 500, build 20, webrtc.fyi 14, reviver 12, codesearch 8, webrtc 8, findit 2, infra 2, trusted.robots 2, flaky-reproducer 1, ssci 1, and six empty dynamic `*.shadow` buckets that exist "for led builds" [cr-buildbucket.cfg; ci.star:73-115]. One clause each for the small ones: reviver reruns *disabled* tests off-peak; flaky-reproducer replays a flaky task; ssci triggers third-party vendoring; build measures Siso/RBE performance; codesearch compiles with Kythe extractors but stops before the kzip upload; trusted.robots (2026-06-16) requests Clang builds in the Lexan instance; infra is the autosharder; findit is LUCI Bisection's rerun fleet. Group counts once: ci = 641 in 30 named groups + 6 group-less; try = 500 in 21 + 9; 55 distinct builder_group values project-wide (dossier R13/V14). OWNED ELSEWHERE: lucicfg mechanics (§02); targets and gn-args resolution (§05); bot_update (§04); orchestrator/compilator (§07); pool sizes (§05).

sections.title: Materialising a checkout
sections.brief:
THESIS: every build on every bot begins with one step called `bot_update`, and it is a three-layer sandwich, not a program.
Layers [depot_tools/recipes/recipe_modules/bot_update/api.py:5,298]. (1) The recipe module `BotUpdateApi` turns a gclient config plus the Buildbucket build input into a command line, runs it as a step named exactly `bot_update`, reads back JSON and translates it into build properties, a Buildbucket output commit and — since November 2025 — a TurboCI `CHECK_KIND_SOURCE` check the compile check depends on [api.py:80-295]. (2) The 1,458-line resource script bot_update.py, which knows nothing about recipes. (3) depot_tools proper: git_cache.py and gclient.py/gclient_scm.py.
The sequence, from the live log of ci/Linux Builder #228485 (2026-09-22) — one observation, say so: `git cat-file -e <pin>` misses → `git cache populate -v --cache-dir ... --reset-fetch-config --no-fetch-tags --commit <pin> --ref refs/heads/main` (0.2 min) → `git clone --no-checkout --local --shared <mirror> [CACHE]/builder/src` with gc.auto/gc.autodetach/gc.autopacklimit at 0 → `git fetch origin <pin>` → `git checkout --force <pin> --` (66 s, cold cache) → `git clean -dff` → `gclient sync ... --revision src@unmanaged` (3.5 min) → `gclient revinfo` (0.4 min). Total 5 min 17 s, 168 git repositories in the manifest, step_text disk usage moving [154GB/290GB used (53%)] → [178GB/290GB used (61%)]; `gclient runhooks` then takes 1 min 42 s [https://logs.chromium.org/logs/chromium/buildbucket/cr-buildbucket/8669979448925519377/+/u/bot_update/stdout].
Mechanisms worth a sentence each. The mirror in [CACHE]/git is bootstrapped from gs://chromium-git-cache/v2/... when missing or when it exceeds GC_AUTOPACKLIMIT = 50 pack files [depot_tools/git_cache.py:29,628-633]. populate retries three times with a 60-second sleep when the pin or a ref is still missing [bot_update.py:795-801]. The script writes its own .gclient pointing at the same cache and syncs with `--verbose --reset --force --upstream --nohooks --noprehooks --delete_unversioned_trees --revision src@unmanaged`: `unmanaged` says the root is already positioned, and `--nohooks` defers DEPS hooks to a separate step so a checkout failure (infra) stays distinguishable from a hook failure (product) [bot_update.py:441-483,960-990]. A GclientSyncFailed wipes the checkout and retries exactly once [bot_update.py:1308-1332].
The patch model, which explains a fact everyone trips on. On try builds the recipe passes `--patch_ref <repo>@<target_ref>:<fetch_ref>`; `apply_patch_ref` cherry-picks `target..patch --keep-redundant-commits` then soft-resets to the base, so the CL is staged, not committed — which is why `got_revision` on a try build is the base commit and not the CL [depot_tools/gclient_scm.py:595-616,812-816]. Patch failures exit 88 and become a red FAILURE with `do_not_retry=true`; `bot_update (without patch)` re-pins every fixed revision and reruns with patch=False, which is what makes DEPS-changing CLs deapply correctly [bot_update/api.py:732-790,997-1027].
Numbers to carry: 3,600 s timeout passed by chromium_tests for CI and try alike; STALE_PROCESS_DURATION 1,200 s with a ps-tree dump every 300 s; GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_LIMIT 102,400 B/s for 1,800 s; exit 88 = patch failure, 87 = patch download failure; git_cache_epoch 1789770839 = 2026-09-18 22:33:59 UTC, four days before the build.
CODE EXCERPTS (2): (a) bot_update.py:822-835 — clone/fetch/checkout/clean; (b) gclient_scm.py:812-816 — cherry-pick plus soft reset. Escape < > & inside <pre>.
OWNED ELSEWHERE: DEPS and gclient semantics generally (sibling post, link ../deps-and-goma/); why bot_update cannot close the tree (§09); the without-patch *test* phase (§07); recipe bundles (§11).

sections.title: What runs, where, on how many machines
sections.brief:
THESIS: test configuration is mid-migration between two generations, the shard count in the tree is not the shard count that runs, and the machines behind it are countable from an anonymous API.
Two generations. Legacy: //testing/buildbot — waterfalls.pyl, test_suite_exceptions.pyl (by design it can only remove or modify, never add) and a 2,625-line generate_buildbot_json.py expanding them into one JSON per waterfall, with a documented layering order and `$$MAGIC_SUBSTITUTION_` hooks for GPU ids and CrOS filter files [buildbot/README.md:29-90; generate_buildbot_json.py:735-864]. Current: Starlark — since 2023-04 the four non-builder-specific pyl files are generated by lucicfg from //infra/config/targets into generated/testing, and since 2024-01 builders set `targets = targets.bundle(...)` directly, so only 16 builder groups and 104 machines remain legacy [targets/README.md:114-141]. The targets package is 20,113 lines: 485 tests, 368 bundles, 329 binaries, 215 mixins.
MB bridges builder identity to GN [tools/mb/mb.py:1213-1348]: it consults gn_args_locations.json and the Starlark gn-args.json first (51 groups / 914 builders), falls back to mb_config.pyl (26 groups / 180 builders), writes args.gn, maps swarming targets to GN labels via gn_isolate_map.pyl (408 entries), and emits the .isolate files the recipe archives to CAS.
Sharding is environmental, then overridden. Tasks are named `<name>:<index>:<count>` with GTEST_SHARD_INDEX / GTEST_TOTAL_SHARDS, and the Test Executable API requires a runner to run every test i where i mod N == M [test_executable_api.md:311-328]. The override is the punchline: the `autosharder` builder (bucket infra, daily 09:00 UTC) queries 14 days of p80 shard runtimes from BigQuery with ≥ 1,500 samples, computes `optimal = ceil(shards × (runtime − overhead) / (15 min − overhead))` floored at 1, rewrites autoshard_exceptions.json and uploads a rubber-stamped auto-submit CL [tools/build recipes/chromium/autosharder.py:96-179; subprojects/infra/subproject.star:73-113]. So `browser_tests` on ci/Linux Tests is `shards = 20` in Starlark [chromium.linux.star:695] and 70 in the generated spec [ci/Linux Tests/targets/chromium.linux.json:239], with autoshard_exceptions.json:118-121 between them; the same file lifts blink_web_tests 8 → 9. Always cite the pair (R11/V12). Linux Tests expands to 86 gtests + 37 isolated scripts = 313 shard tasks.
Results. Since Q4 2021 "all tests on Chrome/Chromium builders have their test results uploaded to ResultDB, and nearly all pass-fail decisions on the builders are based on these results" [resultdb.md:5-12]; harnesses talk to a local ResultSink started by `rdb stream`, its address and token arriving through LUCI_CONTEXT [result_sink.py:31-66].
The fleet, dated; fig-fleet carries the breakdown. On 2026-09-22 (09:45-09:55Z) `luci.chromium.ci` held 590 bots for 490 declared builders, `luci.chromium.try` 2,113 for 382 — mostly builderful, only 513 carry `builderless:1`. Test pools are an order of magnitude larger and breathe with load: chromium.tests 20,320-20,694 bots (24,172 the previous afternoon), 13,180 GCE VMs under the Robocrop autoscaler against 7,395 physical machines in three labs [os_upgrade_playbook.md:337-383; Swarming CountBots]; chromium.tests.gpu is the opposite shape, 3,266 bots of which 3,118 physical. In the 24 h to 2026-09-22T09:59:47Z chromium.tests created 2,417,399 tasks, 210,323 deduped. Caveat: DEDUPED is a form of COMPLETED, so the buckets do not partition the total (C04).
CODE EXCERPTS (2): ci/Linux Tests/targets/chromium.linux.json:219-243 (browser_tests, `"shards": 70`); build/util/lib/results/result_sink.py:31-63. Escape < > & in <pre>.
OWNED ELSEWHERE: retry ladder and exoneration (§07); builder dimensions and gn args (§03); perf shards (§09).

BOTTOM lane (legacy, 16 groups / 104 machines left): waterfalls.pyl + test_suite_exceptions.pyl + the generated pyl → generate_buildbot_json.py (2,625 lines) → testing/buildbot/<group>.json. A vertical override arrow labelled `autoshard_exceptions.json` cuts across both lanes at generation time, carrying the worked example 20 → 70 for browser_tests on ci/Linux Tests (blink_web_tests 8 → 9 beside it) and the autosharder loop beneath it (daily 09:00 UTC, 14-day BigQuery window, p80, ≥ 1,500 samples, ceil(shards × (runtime − overhead) / (15 min − overhead)) floored at 1, rubber-stamped auto-submit CL). sections.title: The commit path, upload to tryjob
sections.brief:
THESIS: between a keystroke and a running tryjob sit five machines and two presubmit runs, and which tryjobs run is decided by a generated file, not a person.
Upload. `git cl upload` runs presubmit_support.py `--upload`, then pushes the squashed commit to Gerrit's magic ref `refs/for/<branch>%<opts>`; changes are WIP unless `--send-mail`, and `-c` / `-d` append `l=Commit-Queue+2` / `l=Commit-Queue+1` as push options [git_cl.py:1935-1996,2210-2253,7205-7218]. `git cl try` votes Commit-Queue+1; with `-B luci.chromium.try -b <builder>` it calls Buildbucket ScheduleBuild directly, tagged `user_agent: git_cl_try` [git_cl.py:414-490,8112-8124]. The docs ask ≤ ~5-10 tryjobs per builder per hour; per-user quotas were never implemented [trybot_usage.md:26-28].
Presubmit. src/PRESUBMIT.py declares `PRESUBMIT_VERSION = '2.0.0'`: presubmit_support then runs every global `Check*` function, skipping `*Commit` on upload and `*Upload` on commit [PRESUBMIT.py:4-23; presubmit_support.py:1797-1811]. The file is 8,937 lines with 95 top-level checks (re-counted locally): banned patterns as `BanRule` dataclasses, `CheckUnwantedDependencies` (checkdeps on added includes; `-` rules error, `!` warn), CheckTodoBugReferences (ids must exceed Monorail's last id 1524553), CheckTreeIsOpenOnCommit, plus depot_tools' holiday infra-freeze windows, bypassable with `Ignore-Freeze` [presubmit_canned_checks.py:1179-1240].
Cloud rerun: `linux-presubmit` / `win-presubmit`, recipe `presubmit`, 40-minute build and 8-minute step timeouts, priority 25 vs the default 30, `on_default_cq`, `disable_reuse`; it runs `--commit --skip_canned CheckTreeIsOpen` because CV checks the tree itself, and uploads findings as ResultDB entries surfaced in Gerrit [try/presubmit.star:27-31,178-220]. Review gates are Gerrit-side: a committer's Code-Review+1 (two if the author is not a committer), an OWNERS approval per file, `Owners-Override+1` for gardeners and release PMs, `Bot-Commit+1` from the Rubber Stamper [docs/code_reviews.md:235-313].
Which tryjobs run. commit-queue.cfg has two config groups: `cq` watches `refs/heads/.+` with committers `project-chromium-submit-access`, dry-runners `project-chromium-tryjob-access`, a `tree_status` verifier and 603 tryjob verifiers; `fallback-cq` (`fallback: YES`) watches every `refs/branch-heads/.*` except the seven active milestone refs and runs one builder, `requires-testing-checker` — 604 entries total, re-verified [commit-queue.cfg:7-31, 9411-9450]. Of the 603, 467 are `includable_only`, 7 carry `experiment_percentage`. cq-builders.md (1,128 lines, "Auto-generated by lucicfg (via cq-builders-md.star)") lists 32 required builders — 28 chromium + 4 chrome — that "must pass before a CL may land that affects files outside of //docs and //infra/config", plus 95 path-based, 7 experimental, 2 mega-cq-launchers. Flag the trap (R01): the `cq` *property* in cr-buildbucket.cfg counts 37 / 92 because it ignores includable_only and experiment_percentage; the blocking set is cq-usage/default.cfg's 32. Every builder carries default exclusions for `infra/config/.+` and `docs/.+` plus an include for its own generated dir.
Reuse is why CQ+1 → CQ+2 feels instant. Each tryjob gets a ReuseKey = sha256 over (CL id, MinEquivalentPatchset, disable-reuse footer values); MinEquivalentPatchset survives NO_CHANGE, NO_CODE_CHANGE, MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE, TRIVIAL_REBASE and TRIVIAL_REBASE_WITH_MESSAGE_UPDATE — only REWORK forks it [cv/internal/tryjob/execute/reuse_common.go:192-220; cv/internal/gerrit/equi.go:24-76]. Default window `staleTryjobAge = 24h`; since 2026-07-27 CV can instead compare the build's output Cr-Commit-Position with the branch tip, enabled 2026-09-18 for one builder only, `linux_chromium_compile_dbg_ng`, `max_commit_distance` 800 on main [reuse_common.go:116-177; tryserver.chromium.linux.star:888-891]. Worked example: CL 8423730's dry run was reused 14.4 hours later for 32 of 34 tryjobs; the two fresh launches were the presubmit builders (`disable_reuse`; 12 builders set it).

sections.title: Inside a CQ build
sections.brief:
THESIS: a CQ build is not one build, and a test failure is not a verdict. The orchestrator/compilator split and the four-phase retry ladder exist for one measured reason: "the CQ has roughly ~20,000 unique flaky tests" [docs/infra/cq.md:343-352]. Structure first. `linux-rel` runs recipe `chromium/orchestrator` on 2-4 cores, mirrors ci/Linux Builder, Linux Tests, GPU Linux Builder and Linux Release (NVIDIA), and delegates compile and isolate to `linux-rel-compilator`, the ≥ 16-core machine [builder_types.md:159-187; try/tryserver.chromium.linux.star:453-499]. Give the four builder_types.md patterns one sentence each — all-in-one local, all-in-one swarmed, builder/tester split, orchestrator/compilator — and say why the last exists: the expensive machine is held only while compiling. The ladder, quoted from the docs then made concrete [docs/infra/cq.md:243-262]: compile the affected suites; run them `(with patch)` as sharded Swarming tasks; retry the failed shards identically as `(retry shards with patch)`; recompile without the CL and rerun only the failures as `(without patch)`; fail the build only for tests that failed in both patched phases but passed without the patch. Constants: the without-patch phase repeats each failing test 10 times with retry limit 0 and runs only when ≤ 100 tests need retrying; CI builders instead retry shards with the limit raised to 5; the retry filter is capped at 6,000 characters on Windows and 90,000 elsewhere; the default retry limit is 3 [tools/build chromium_tests/steps.py:81-85,229-245; test_executable_api.md:168-171]. Exoneration is the second subtraction. The recipe queries LUCI Analysis per failing variant and records ResultDB `TestExoneration`s with reasons OCCURS_ON_MAINLINE, OCCURS_ON_OTHER_CLS or NOT_CRITICAL [tools/build test_utils/api.py]. Thresholds: failure_threshold 6, consecutive_failure_threshold 3, flake_threshold 3 [luci-analysis.cfg:165-176]. Bug-filing thresholds live in the same file but a different field, and the dossier had to adjudicate this (R12): lines 4-15 are the legacy top-level `bug_filing_thresholds` (75 exonerations in 3 days; 10 builds in 7 days); lines 80-163 are the `bug_management.policies` activation thresholds (30 in 3 days with a 1-in-7-days deactivation; 7 builds in 3 days; 10 CL rejections in 1 day at P0). Say which field you are quoting. Cancellation and quotas, briefly: a new patchset always cancels the Run, but only a REWORK cancels the running builds, and two builders set `cancel_stale: NO` (win-arm64-compile-dbg, win_chromium_compile_dbg_ng) [commit-queue.cfg:8489,9098]. CV's retry_config is single_quota 1, global_quota 2, timeout_weight 2 [commit-queue.cfg:9354-9360]. Active runs per user: 10 by default, 20 for chromium-src-increased-quota, unlimited for the emergency group and the Skia autoroller [commit-queue.cfg:9375-9407]. Try builds expire after 2 hours pending [try.star:18-20]. Close honestly: three of the four phases exist to distinguish "your change is broken" from "this test is broken", and the cost is that a CQ run can compile the tree twice. The 40-minute median / ~1-hour p90 cycle-time bar for adding a builder to the CQ [cq.md:304-305] is the budget shaping every one of these constants. sections.title: From green to refs/heads/main
sections.brief:
THESIS: there is no commit-numbering daemon. Sequential Cr-Commit-Position numbers fall out of three independent mechanisms — CV's single-submitter queue, Gerrit's REBASE_ALWAYS submit type, and a Gerrit plugin with a three-line rule. The three machines (§1.12). CV owns the Run; Gerrit owns the merge (chromium/src's submit type is REBASE_ALWAYS with content merge inherited on); the git-numberer plugin owns numbering. The commit is authored by the CL owner and *committed* by CV's project-scoped identity chromium-scoped@luci-project-accounts.iam.gserviceaccount.com — 397 of the last 400 main commits in the sample; the other three were direct human submits. Run states, from the proto: PENDING → RUNNING → WAITING_FOR_SUBMISSION → SUBMITTING → SUCCEEDED | FAILED | CANCELLED, with WAITING_FOR_SUBMISSION cancellable, SUBMITTING not, and a 10-day force-cancel [cv/internal/run/storage.proto:30-73; cv/internal/common/run.go:39]. The submit queue. `OnReadyForSubmission` acquires a per-LUCI-project SubmitQueue — one datastore entity with a Current run, a FIFO waitlist and a History of recent submissions — then checks the tree; OPEN and THROTTLED both count as open, a closed tree releases the slot and pokes again after a minute, and more than 10 minutes of status-service errors fails the Run [run/impl/handler/submit.go:52-184; run/impl/submit/queue.go:38-90]. Burst pacing lives in that queue: chromium sets `submit_max_burst = 2` with a one-minute delay [main.star:144-149, verified locally; commit-queue.cfg:8-12]. The measurement that makes it real: over 400 consecutive main commits, no three CV-committed commits fell inside 60 seconds — the only 3-in-60s windows each contained a direct human submit. Main's commit rate over the sampled 12.6-hour window was 31.8/h. Submission is Gerrit `SubmitRevision` per CL with 10 exponential retries from a 200 ms base; a 409 FailedPrecondition is permanent and produces the familiar "Cannot rebase … could not be rebased due to a conflict during merge" message, CQ vote removed [submitter.go:161-169,224-347]. The per-Run submission deadline is 20 minutes, 40 for CrOS kernel changes [handler/submit.go:506-523]. Why REBASE_ALWAYS matters beyond history shape: Gerrit only invokes ChangeMessageModifier plugins for the Rebase Always and Cherry Pick strategies, so numbering works only because the commit is rewritten at submit [gerrit Documentation/dev-plugins.txt] — the causal chain is reconstruction, each link sourced. git-numberer's rule is three lines: a new commit C has at most one parent P; P carries `Cr-Commit-Position: refs/foo/bar@{#X}`; C gets `@{#X+1}`. A different destination ref yields `@{#1}` plus `Cr-Branched-From`, and a validator rejects merge commits, non-fast-forwards and wrong lineage on every push and submit [git-numberer README:11-18]. Correct the folklore (R15): "daemon" is a leftover from the pre-Gerrit era. Auto-Submit is likewise not a CV feature: the `chromium-behavior` Gerrit frontend plugin rewrites a reviewer's Code-Review+1 into CR+1 *and* CQ+2 when Auto-Submit+1 is set, and the Rubber Stamper does the same from the bot side; the owner, not the voting reviewer, pays the run quota [chromium-behavior web/autosubmit.ts:225-298; prjmanager/triager/runs.go quotaPayer]. Anchor: main was at Cr-Commit-Position 1702467 on 2026-09-22 10:20:39 UTC (fed5391984ac); the reference tree f288fed6 is @{#1701190}. sections.title: The waterfall and its humans
sections.brief:
THESIS: the post-submit half is a fan-out, a regexp, twelve rotations and a bisection service — and the regexp holds a fossil that cannot fire. Fan-out. `chromium-gitiles-trigger` polls refs/heads/main and fans each commit to 386 CI builders; the rest of the 641 in ci are triggered by their parents from inside the recipe, via a scheduler GitilesTrigger carrying `parent_got_*` properties and `deps_revision_overrides` [luci-scheduler.cfg:6647-7039; chromium_tests/api.py trigger_child_builds]. That is §03's builder/tester split, seen from the scheduler. The tree. 133 of those builders are tree closers (re-verified against 252 notifiers). LUCI Notify closes the tree when a *failing step* matches `\b(bot_update|compile|gclient runhooks|generate_build_files|runhooks|update|\w*nocompile_test)\b` [notifiers.star:85-125]. The subtlety: Notify only reacts to builds ending SUCCESS or FAILURE, and because `bot_update` runs with `infra_step=True` a broken checkout is a purple INFRA_FAILURE that cannot close the tree — in practice `gclient runhooks` does [notify.go:302-426; bot_update/api.py:309]. Flag the open question: no recipe path was found that runs bot_update with infra_step=False, so the entry is a Buildbot-era holdover, like `update` (Part 9, item 24) reconstruction. Closure is asymmetric: a manually closed tree is never reopened by a bot; an auto-closed one reopens when closers pass or a culprit revert lands [tree_status.go]. The host is a facade: chromium-status.appspot.com proxies GetStatus/ListStatus to LUCI Tree Status, which returned an identical record on 2026-09-20 (R10/V11). The humans. Twelve gardener rotations, renamed from "sheriffs" in May 2023 — chromium 141 builders, chromium.gpu 94, dawn 56, chromium.clang 46, android 43 — who keep the tree open and may revert with Owners-Override and the Rubber Stamper; shifts are 8 hours [sheriff-rotations/*.txt; gardener.md:3-63]. The automation beside them. LUCI Bisection, "formerly GoFindit … the rewrite in Golang of the Python2 version of Findit", runs nth-section bisection and culprit verification on findit's two builders. For compile failures it may create 10 reverts a day and auto-submit 4, only for culprits younger than 21,600 s, voting Owners-Override+1, Bot-Commit+1 and Commit-Queue+2; test-failure reverts are created but never submitted [luci-bisection.cfg:4-54]. It refuses autoroller authors, `NOAUTOREVERT=true`, culprits with merged dependents, and ungardened builders [revertculprit/createrevert.go]. Note the 2026 layer without over-claiming: the tree-closure e-mail template says "GardenerAI is currently attempting to identify and revert the culprit"; no public design doc exists (Part 9, item 13). H3 "The other waterfall" (~150 words). Performance CI is a separate pipeline in the internal `chrome` project; public enumeration is src-side only: chromium.perf.json holds 71 entries — 18 `*-builder-perf`, 46 testers, 7 `*-processor-perf` — exposing 628 shards across 39 primary lab platforms [perf_waterfall.md:17-42]. Builders POST each isolate's CAS digest to Pinpoint's /api/isolate so bisects reuse waterfall builds; testers run continuously, covering commits since the previous run's end. Enforcement is social, not a required builder — except size: `android-binary-size` (16 KB arm32 / 64 KB arm64 / 50 dex methods), `compile-size` (200 MiB) and `fuchsia-binary-size` are `cq: required`, bypassable only with a `Binary-Size:`/`Compile-Size:` footer [android_binary_size_trybot.md:27-30]. sections.title: The release cycle and the branches
sections.brief:
THESIS: the release process is legible from git, and the biggest 2026 fact is that the cadence changed. Do not repeat the four-week folklore.
The cadence. docs/process/release_cycle.md, rewritten 2026-08-26: a milestone is developed on main for two weeks, branched, stabilised for three weeks, shipped, then refreshed weekly; Extended Stable maintains every *fourth* milestone six extra weeks, so an ES milestone still ships every eight weeks [release_cycle.md:8-26, verified locally]. Announced 2026-03-03; effective with Chrome 153's stable release on 2026-09-08 [developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-two-week-release]. History: ~6 weeks from July 2010, 4 weeks from Chrome 94 (announced 2021-03-04, stable 2021-09-21), 2 from Chrome 153. chromium.org's "chrome-release-channels" page still says every 4 weeks (Part 9, item 29).
The seam, from chromiumdash: M152 (7977) branched 2026-07-27, shipped 08-25 on the old rhythm; M153 (8010) branched 08-17, shipped 09-08; then M154 (8037), M155 (8059), M156 every two weeks, M160 at 2027-01-05 after a holiday stretch.
Version semantics. chrome/VERSION is four KEY=VALUE lines; at f288fed6, MAJOR=156 MINOR=0 BUILD=8067 PATCH=0 (verified locally). On trunk, BUILD is bumped twice on weekdays (about 03:01 and 14:01 UTC) by chrome-official-brancher@chops-service-accounts: "This is an automated release commit. Do not revert without consulting chrome-pmo@google.com. NOAUTOREVERT=true". The MAJOR bump *is* branch day, so a milestone's branch number equals its last trunk BUILD — M153 = 8010, M154 = 8037, M155 = 8059 — and a two-week milestone spans ~22 BUILD numbers where a four-week one spanned ~50. Correct one folklore item (R07): "Chrome Release Bot (LUCI)" was only chrome-official-brancher's display name; no account change happened.
Every trunk BUILD number gets its own ref. On refs/branch-heads/8067, @{#1} is "Create chrome_branch_deps.json for branch 8067." (2026-09-21 12:40:19 UTC), @{#2} "Incrementing VERSION to 156.0.8067.1", @{#3} 8067.2, all carrying `Cr-Branched-From main@{#1701636}` (R05). On branches, PATCH increments via "Incrementing VERSION" commits carrying `Merge-Approval-Bypass: Chrome release infra`, DEPS advance via "Roll commits from side projects in M155", and each stable rollout ships two builds differing only in PATCH, for A/B. Date the older mechanism (C09/R08): per-build branches switched from "Publish DEPS for X" to chrome_branch_deps.json on 2023-06-29, branches 5860 → 5861.
Branch day is a config event, tying back to §02. chrome-branch-day@chops-service-accounts lands "Activate chromium M155" on main (adding it to milestones.json) and "Update LUCI config for M155" on the branch — 3,019 files — rewriting settings.json to project `chromium-m155`, ref `refs/branch-heads/8059`, `is_main: false`, seven beta/stable platforms. The branch's config then holds 256 builders in 30,255 lines against trunk's 1,211 in 139,286, because every builder carries a `branch_selector` branches.star matches against the project's platforms [scripts/branch.py:102-126; milestones.json, verified locally]. milestones.json lists seven active milestones — 144, 150-155 — M144/M150 alive for ChromeOS LTS, not Extended Stable (R09).
Merges are main-first: a `Merge-Request` field on the bug creates a Merge Request issue within the hour, release managers answer within two business days, then the fix lands by Gerrit Cherry Pick or `git cl cherry-pick --branch=refs/branch-heads/####`, the Rubber Stamper able to Bot-Commit one within 14 days [merge_request.md:43-44,207-212,345-370].

sections.title: The release scripts
sections.brief:
THESIS: the scripts that ship a browser are small, old and deliberately boring — Step classes with a JSON resume file, a regex over four #define lines, a hook writing one string into a header. The engineering is what surrounds them.
V8, in v8/tools/release/. common_includes.py (Copyright 2013) gives every script a list of `Step` classes, a JSON state file so `-s N` resumes, git retry wait-plans ([5, 30] s; [10, 30, 60×5] s when waiting for a landed commit to replicate) and a regex reader for the four #define lines in include/v8-version.h [common_includes.py:283-562; v8-version.h:8-18 — verified at 15.6.0, candidate 1]. create_release.py is the daily push: take lkgr, compute the next version as max(main, latest tag), build+1, patch 0, push it as refs/heads/<x.y.z>, rewrite the version header (candidate 0), un-comment the v8-merges@ WATCHLIST entry, land `--bypass-hooks -f`, tag [create_release.py:41-57,139-159; auto_push.py:42-61]. Rolling into Chromium is two-stage: `detect_roll_candidate` scans the 160 newest tags for the newest version with a matching `-pgo` tag (patched versions get a 3-hour priority window) and force-pushes it to refs/heads/roll; Skia's `v8-chromium-autoroll` (BATCH) turns that into "Roll V8 from A to B" CLs with 50 try jobs. Back-merges go through Gerrit's REST API, not local git (merge_to_branch_gerrit.py:92-107): roll_merge_gerrit.py bumps V8_PATCH_LEVEL via a change-edit, adds Owners-Override+1 and the rubber stamper, submits, tags, waits 15-20 min for the -pgo tag [roll_merge_gerrit.py:154-175].
Chromium's own two. build/util/version.py substitutes `@KEY@` placeholders from VERSION, BRANDING and LASTCHANGE into templates and derives Android versionCodes [version.py:44-66; android_chrome_version.py:37-44,76]. build/util/lastchange.py, a DEPS hook, writes `LASTCHANGE=<hash>-<Cr-Commit-Position>` by reading the footer out of the commit object; non-official builds read LASTCHANGE.dummy and stay reproducible [lastchange.py:166-188; version.py:59-64, verified]. That joins §08's numbering to the About box.
Packaging is vestigial — FILES.cfg replaced by infra/archive_config/*.json — except on Windows: chrome/tools/build/win/create_installer_archive.py stages chrome.release, builds chrome.7z, compresses it with hand-tuned BCJ2/LZMA flags (~2.3 MB + ~3.5 MB saved) or a bsdiff/Zucchini patch, packs setup.ex_ with makecab.py, emits packed_files.rc [create_installer_archive.py:85-92,434-456,516-536].
Toolchain rolls are where a human still sits: tools/clang/scripts/upload_revision.py rewrites CLANG_REVISION and the Rust revisions, uploads `--bypass-hooks` and fires the `*_upload_clang` / `*_upload_rust` trybots, which run package.py --upload into a staging bucket with `x-goog-if-generation-match:0`; a Googler promotes, then sync_deps.py rewrites the GCS DEPS entries [upload_revision.py:444-462; updating_clang.md:14-62].
Close with the third propagation path (§1.15, ~180 words). (a) Recipes: every commit to chromium/tools/build becomes a CIPD bundle (`recipes.py fetch`, `recipes.py bundle`, `cipd create -tag git_revision:<sha> -ref <ref>`), latency 0.7-4.2 min over 12 instances; only refs/heads/main still moves (479 chromium/NNNN refs frozen since 2020-11-16); the autoroller runs every 10 minutes: 163 roll CLs in 30 days, 122 merged, 41 abandoned. (b) Configs: §02. (c) Binaries: the bootstrapper is Go for 7 platforms uploaded `-ref latest`; because the build is reproducible an unchanged binary re-registers as the *same* instance (210 tag pairs over 7.4 days), so `latest` moves only when the bytes change — no canary. bbagent is pinned in Buildbucket service settings instead, with a version_canary chromium's try bucket takes at 5 %.
CODE EXCERPTS (2): v8/tools/release/create_release.py:41-57; build/util/lastchange.py:166-188.
OWNED ELSEWHERE: branch-day regeneration (§10); DEPS (../deps-and-goma/); lucicfg (§02); bot_update (§04).

sections.title: What the pipeline optimises for
sections.brief: THESIS: close by naming the objective function and the places it leaves for people. No summary of the post; four claims, each with its evidence, then an honest boundary. Claim 1 — it optimises for reviewability of the infrastructure, not deployment speed. Nothing is deployed: a builder, a shard count, a CQ membership and a release branch's builder set are all CLs in chromium/src, guarded by the same presubmit and the same commit queue as product code, reaching the services through a polling importer with a validation gate (§02). The cost is a 1-11 minute floor on any config change and a 53 MB generated tree that must be regenerated and diffed on every CL. Claim 2 — it optimises for reuse over recomputation. The 24-hour ReuseKey window, the 210,323 deduped Swarming tasks in a single day, the bootstrapper reading properties at the built revision, CIPD re-registering an unchanged binary as the same instance: the system would rather prove a result still valid than compute it again (§06, §05, §11). Claim 3 — it optimises for keeping the tree green and accepts spending compute to do it. Three of the four CQ phases exist to distinguish a broken change from a broken test, against a documented ~20,000 unique flaky tests; 133 tree closers, twelve gardener rotations and a bisection service with a daily revert budget sit on the other side of submit (§07, §09). Claim 4 — it optimises for a system that can be branched. branch_selector, milestones.json and settings.json mean the same Starlark produces trunk's 1,211 builders and M155's 256; the release machinery is the CI machinery with a filter applied (§10). Where the humans still sit, concretely: an OWNERS approval per file and a committer's Code-Review+1 (§06); a gardener with Owners-Override and an 8-hour shift (§09); release managers with a two-business-day merge-request SLO (§10); the Googler who promotes a staged clang package out of the `x-goog-if-generation-match:0` bucket (§11); the owner who must approve a nontrivial recipe roll (one measured wait of 8 h 39 m); and whoever is in chromium-src-emergency-quota when the CQ needs to be told the rules do not apply. Then the boundary, as a short list, so the reader knows where the teardown stops: the internal `chrome` project's config (perf builders, the linux-perf-trigger / win-perf-trigger definitions), the fleet-side infradata/config behind the 2026-09-20..22 NO_RESOURCE incident (26,001 builds in one day against a 150-731 baseline), the internal automation behind chrome-official-brancher and chrome-branch-day, what GardenerAI is, what TurboCI is precisely (100 % on 234 builders, observable only as CHECK_KIND_SOURCE and BUILD checks), and the semantics of the `Skip-Performance-Test` footer, which appears in no public repository. Mark these reconstruction or "not verified" as appropriate. No number may appear here that was not sourced earlier in the post; every figure cell points back to a section. OWNED ELSEWHERE: everything. This section cites, it does not introduce.

Rows: config in the tree (reviewable, bisectable, branchable ↔ 1-11 min propagation floor and 53 MB of generated diff ↔ the infra/config OWNERS layers); reuse by key (CQ+1 → CQ+2 near-instant, 210,323 deduped tasks/day ↔ a 24-hour window means a stale green ↔ the 12 builders that opt out with disable_reuse); retry then exonerate (a green tree despite ~20,000 flaky tests ↔ a CQ run can compile the tree twice ↔ gardeners and the bug-filing thresholds); bootstrapper indirection (a CL tests its own property change ↔ orchestrator and compilator can run different recipe revisions ↔ nontrivial recipe rolls wait for an owner); branch_selector (1,211 → 256 builders with no fork ↔ branch projects run trunk recipes with branch-pinned properties ↔ release managers and the merge-request SLO).
